questions.title: Print 1 through N
questions.description: Read an integer n from input(). Print each number from 1 through n on its own line. For n = 0, print nothing. Constraint: 0 <= n <= 100.
questions.starterCode:
n = int(input())
# Write your loop here
questions.hint: Think about which endpoint range includes and which it excludes.
questions.revision: Trace the first and last iteration of a loop. Compare range(n) and range(1, n + 1). Practise n = 0, 1, and 5.

questions.title: Sum Array Values
questions.description: Implement solve(nums) and return the sum of the integers. An empty list has sum 0. Constraints: at most 100 values, each between -1000 and 1000.
questions.starterCode:
def solve(nums):
    total = 0
    # Write your code here
    return total
questions.hint: Keep a running total, then return it after processing the list.
questions.revision: Trace an accumulator over an array. Check an empty list and negative values. Explain why a return inside the loop changes the result.

questions.title: Reverse a String
questions.description: Implement solve(text) and return the characters in reverse order. Keep spaces and letter case. Input length is at most 100.
questions.hint: Try reading the indices from the last character to the first.
questions.revision: Review string indexing, slices, and immutable strings. Test the empty string and a string containing spaces.

questions.title: Find the Largest Value
questions.description: Implement solve(nums) and return the largest integer in a non-empty list. Constraints: 1 to 100 values; negative values are allowed.
questions.starterCode:
def solve(nums):
    largest = nums[0]
    # Write your code here
    return largest
questions.hint: Your initial largest value must also work when every value is negative.
questions.revision: Review initial values and loop invariants. After processing each element, largest should be the maximum of all elements seen.

questions.title: Count Vowels
questions.description: Implement solve(text). Count a, e, i, o, u, including uppercase versions. All input characters are ASCII, and length is at most 100.
questions.starterCode:
def solve(text):
    count = 0
    # Write your code here
    return count
questions.hint: Normalize the character case before checking membership in the vowel set.
questions.revision: Review string membership and case conversion. Distinguish testing membership from comparing against a whole string.

questions.title: Find a Sorted Target
questions.description: Implement solve(nums, target). The integers are sorted and distinct. Return the target index or -1 if absent. Use binary search for O(log n) work. At most 100 values. These output tests do not prove complexity.
questions.starterCode:
def solve(nums, target):
    left = 0
    right = len(nums) - 1
    # Write your code here
    return -1
questions.hint: State which endpoints are inclusive and make the search interval smaller after each comparison.
questions.revision: Trace left, right, and mid. For an inclusive interval, discard a checked midpoint using mid + 1 or mid - 1. Test empty and one-element lists.

questions.title: Check a Palindrome
questions.description: Implement solve(text) and return a Boolean indicating whether text equals its reverse. Comparison is case-sensitive and includes spaces. An empty string is a palindrome. Length is at most 100.
questions.hint: Compare the two ends, then move inward.
questions.revision: Review the stopping condition for two pointers. A mismatch disproves a palindrome; matching just the first pair does not prove one.

questions.title: Match Brackets
questions.description: Implement solve(text). Input contains only ()[]{}. Return true if brackets are balanced and correctly nested, otherwise false. The empty string is balanced. Length is at most 100.
questions.hint: The most recent unmatched opening bracket must match the next closing bracket.
questions.revision: Review last-in-first-out order. Check for an empty stack before popping, and check for unmatched opening brackets at the end.

questions.title: Compute a Factorial
questions.description: Implement solve(n) to return n factorial. By definition, 0! = 1. Constraint: 0 <= n <= 10. Practise a recursive solution; output tests also accept an iterative solution.
questions.hint: Relate n! to (n - 1)! and identify the smallest input.
questions.revision: Review base cases and progress toward them. Trace the return values of calls for n = 0, 1, and 3.

questions.title: Best Contiguous Sum
questions.description: Implement solve(nums) and return the largest sum of a non-empty contiguous subarray. Input is a non-empty list of at most 100 integers from -100 to 100.
questions.hint: At each position, decide whether to start again or extend the previous subarray.
questions.revision: Separate the best sum ending here from the best sum anywhere. Initialize from actual data so that an all-negative list works.

questions.title: Longest Unique Window
questions.description: Implement solve(text) and return the length of the longest contiguous substring without repeated characters. Characters are case-sensitive. Length is at most 100.
questions.hint: Move the left boundary until the current window contains no duplicate characters.
questions.revision: Track character positions or counts. The left boundary should never move backward. Trace abba and an empty string.

questions.title: Count Stair Routes
questions.description: Implement solve(n). You may climb 1 or 2 steps at a time. Return the number of ordered ways to reach step n. There is one way to climb 0 steps: do nothing. Constraint: 0 <= n <= 20.
questions.hint: The last move reaches n from either n - 1 or n - 2.
questions.revision: Define each DP state and its base cases. Check n = 0 and n = 1 before filling later states.
